facts.statement: Megalolamna lived from the Late Oligocene to the Middle Miocene, approximately 23.5 to 15 million years ago.
facts.quote: Megalolamna is an extinct genus of large mackerel shark that lived approximately 23.5 to 15 million years ago (Mya), from the Late Oligocene to the Middle Miocene epochs.

facts.statement: Fossils of Megalolamna have been found in the Americas, Europe, and Japan.
facts.quote: Fossils belonging to this genus are known from the Americas, Europe and Japan

facts.statement: Megalolamna could reach a maximum length of 5.1 meters, similar to the modern great white shark.
facts.quote: Although having a maximum length estimated at 5.1 m, a measurement similar to that of the current great white shark

facts.statement: Despite its size, Megalolamna fed only on medium-sized prey.
facts.quote: Megalolamna would have only fed on medium-sized prey

facts.statement: Megalolamna used its front teeth to seize prey and lateral corner teeth to cut it.
facts.quote: The front teeth of Megalolamna would have had the function of seizing the prey, before cutting it using the lateral teeth located at the corner of the mouth

facts.statement: Megalolamna had a cosmopolitan distribution and primarily inhabited shallow waters from tropical to mid-latitude regions.
facts.quote: Fossils proves that the genus had a cosmopolitan distribution and show that it inhabited mainly in shallow environments from tropical to mid-latitude areas

facts.statement: The genus Megalolamna was formally described in 2016 by Kensu Shimada and colleagues based on five fossil teeth found in the US, Japan, and Peru.
facts.quote: It is on the basis of many unifying common points that the new genus and species Megalolamna paradoxodon is described by Japanese paleontologist Kensu Shimada and his colleagues in 2016 from five isolated fossil teeth having been discovered in the United States, Japan and Peru

facts.statement: The genus name Megalolamna combines the Greek word for 'big' with the name of the genus Lamna.
facts.quote: The genus name Megalolamna derives from the Ancient Greek word μεγάλος (megálos, "big"), in combination with Lamna

facts.statement: The species name paradoxodon means 'paradoxical tooth' and refers to the unusual appearance of the shark's teeth.
facts.quote: The specific name parodoxodon comes from the Latin paradoxum, "paradox", and the Ancient Greek ὀδούς (odoús, "tooth"), and refers to what the authors describe as "its paradoxical appearance of teeth"

facts.statement: The holotype for Megalolamna is a complete tooth cataloged as UCMP 112146, discovered in Kern County, California.
facts.quote: The designated holotype of the genus is a complete tooth cataloged as UCMP 112146, having been discovered in Kern County, California

facts.statement: A 2024 study extended the known time range of Megalolamna to the Late Oligocene (23.5 million years ago) based on a tooth from South Carolina.
facts.quote: In 2024, Shimada and colleagues describe three teeth from South Carolina and Maryland. The single tooth from South Carolina extends the taxon's distribution era to the Late Oligocene, at about 23.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: Teeth found in Maryland represent the northernmost known occurrences of Megalolamna.
facts.quote: The two teeth from Maryland embody the northernmost known occurrences of Megalolamna.

facts.statement: The first tooth of this species was described in 1879 by Josef Probst as Otodus serotinus from a fossil found in Baltringen, Germany.
facts.quote: The German tooth having been discovered in the east of Baltringen, in the state of Baden-Württemberg, was the first to be named, being originally described in 1879 by Josef Probst as Otodus serotinus.

facts.statement: Megalolamna belongs to the family Otodontidae, which includes the megalodon.
facts.quote: It is a member of the Otodontidae, a family of large-toothed sharks known to include the contemporary megalodon.

facts.statement: It remains uninvestigated whether the specific names Otodus serotinus and Lamna bassanii are synonyms.
facts.quote: no researchers have visibly looked into the potential synonymy between them

facts.statement: Megalolamna teeth featured a pointed main cusp, upward-pointing lateral cusplets of similar size, and a strongly bilobed root.
facts.quote: The teeth of Megalolamna have the basic features of a lamniform, but are mainly distinguished by the presence of a pointed main cusp sometimes inclined laterally, lateral cusplets (small enameled cusps that appear at the base of the tooth's main crown) about equal in size and pointing upwards, and with a strongly bilobed root.

facts.statement: The largest known Megalolamna tooth measured 4.5 cm in height, while the smallest measured 8.2 mm.
facts.quote: The largest known tooth measures 4.5 cm in height, while the smallest documented measures 8.2 mm.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Megalolamna seized prey with front teeth and then cut it with lateral teeth at the mouth corners to fit it for swallowing.
facts.quote: Thus, the animal probably seized its prey with the front teeth, before cutting it with the lateral teeth located at the corners of the mouth to an acceptable proportion for ingestion.

facts.statement: A more conservative size estimate places the largest known Megalolamna specimen at an average of 5.1 meters, similar to a great white shark.
facts.quote: A second, smaller range gives between 3.7 to 7.2 m, calculating an average length of 5.1 m for the largest known specimen, which is a similar size to a typical great white shark.

facts.statement: The genus Megalolamna was described by Shimada et al. in 2016.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Shimada et al., 2016

facts.statement: The only known species in the genus is Megalolamna paradoxodon.
facts.quote: species: †M. paradoxodon

facts.statement: The species Megalolamna paradoxodon was named by Shimada et al. in 2016.
facts.quote: binomial_authority: Shimada et al., 2016

facts.statement: Megalolamna is considered the sister genus to Otodus.
facts.quote: Es considerado como el género hermano de Otodus.

facts.statement: Megalolamna fossils date to the Miocene epoch.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Mioceno

facts.statement: Megalolamna lived from the Rupelian to the Messinian stages, between 33.9 and 5.333 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rupelian to Messinian (33.9 to 5.333 million years ago)

facts.statement: Megalolamna fossils have been found in early Miocene strata in Peru, Japan, California, and North Carolina.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles se han encontrado en estratos que datan del Mioceno temprano de Perú, Japón y los estados de California y Carolina del Norte en Estados Unidos

facts.statement: Fossil evidence indicates that Megalolamna had a cosmopolitan distribution.
facts.quote: Megalolamna fossils proves that the genus had a cosmopolitan distribution.

facts.statement: The geographical distribution of Megalolamna is similar to that of modern lamniform sharks like the goblin shark, megamouth shark, and Bigeye sand tiger.
facts.quote: This geographical distribution is quite similar to that of many current lamniforms such as the goblin shark, the megamouth shark or the Bigeye sand tiger.

facts.statement: Most Megalolamna fossils come from shallow marine environments, though some suggest it also lived in cold, subtropical waters.
facts.quote: A large majority of the geological formations from which Megalolamna is documented would have been shallow marine environments, although some fossils also suggest that the animal also lived in cold, subtropical waters.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Megalolamna had one or multiple rows of teeth, as its dentition shows a continuous series without clear differences between upper and lower jaws.
facts.quote: Although it is very uncertain whether Megalolamna had one or more rows of teeth in the jaws, its teeth show an almost continuous series of dentition ranging from tall, symmetrical teeth to short, sloping teeth, with no notable differences that would indicate their location in the upper or lower jaw.

facts.statement: Researchers note that the relationship between Megalolamna and Otodus is problematic due to a 43-million-year gap in their appearance.
facts.quote: The authors note, however, that the fact that Megalolamna and Otodus are related is not without problems, because there is a gap in appearance of about 43 million years each.

rejected.statement: Megalolamna likely fed on medium-sized fish ranging from 0.5 to 1 meter in length.
rejected.quote: The estimated body length of the animal also indicates that it fed on medium-sized fish, ranging from 0.5 to 1 m.
